RESEARCH ONLY. Do not write code or create .md report files. Return findings as your final message text.

I need the FULL, VERBATIM-QUOTED legal/policy text from Thunderstore (https://thunderstore.io) relevant to a third party that wants to (a) index/mirror package metadata + icons in their own catalog UI, and (b) download package .zip files server-side and install them into customers' game servers (a paid game-server hosting panel).

Fetch and quote the relevant sections from ALL of these (use WebFetch; also try curl via Bash with `curl -s <url>` and strip HTML with python3 if WebFetch is blocked or summarizes too aggressively — I need EXACT QUOTES, not paraphrase):

1. https://thunderstore.io/tos/
2. Any ToS subpages — look for links on /tos/ such as /tos/terms-of-service/, /tos/acceptable-use/, /tos/content-policy/, /tos/privacy-policy/, /tos/dmca/, /tos/api-terms/ or similar. Enumerate and fetch each one you find.
3. https://thunderstore.io/package/create/docs/ — the package format / manifest.json spec. I need the EXACT list of manifest.json fields (is there a `license` field? quote the spec). Also quote anything about README requirements and whether a license must be declared.
4. Search for and fetch any Thunderstore developer/API documentation about acceptable API use, rate limits, required User-Agent, mirroring, or caching. Check https://thunderstore.io/api/docs/, the Thunderstore GitHub (https://github.com/thunderstore-io), and their wiki/docs site if one exists.

SPECIFIC QUESTIONS — answer each with a direct quote + URL, or explicitly say "not found / not addressed":
A. Does the ToS contain a mandatory LICENSE GRANT from uploaders to Thunderstore and/or to downstream users/third parties for redistribution? Quote it in full.
B. What is the default/assumed license of an uploaded package if the author declares nothing? Is there one?
C. Does the ToS say anything about API usage, automated access, scraping, indexing, mirroring, rate limits, or attribution requirements? Quote.
D. Is there any restriction on COMMERCIAL use — e.g. a paid hosting company using the API/packages as part of a paid product? Quote.
E. What is Thunderstore's stated position on third-party mod managers/launchers (r2modman, Gale, Overwolf, etc.) that auto-download packages? Thunderstore ships its own "Thunderstore Mod Manager" — is there any statement blessing, tolerating, or restricting third-party ones? Look at their GitHub org, their blog/news, and any developer docs.
F. Any DMCA / takedown / content-liability language a third party redistributing content should know about.
G. Note if thunderstore.io/tos/ returns a Cloudflare 403 to curl — if so use WebFetch instead and say so.

Be precise. Quote exactly, always cite the URL the quote came from. If a page does not exist (404), say so explicitly rather than inventing content.

 Structure 
 The readme supports markdown syntax, closely but not exactly matching that of GitHub's. You can view GitHub markdown docs here and general markdown docs here .

 The readme has to be UTF-8 compatible (use Notepad++ or VS Code to check for encoding if you aren't sure). If you're using a new enough version of Windows, you can also check the encoding while saving the file:

 UTF-8 Is generally compatible with other encodings, as many of them share a similar structure for common characters. Generally you will only hit encoding issues if special characters are involved, in which case converting to UTF-8 should solve the issue.

 The markdown preview tool is unable to check for file encoding, as that is a property of the file save format, and the validator does not read files.

 The manifest.json file is what tells Thunderstore and other tools some critical technical information about your package (such as the name & version). Some of it may also be used for presentation.
 The file should be in standard JSON format (UTF-8 encoded) with the following contents:
 Key
 Description

 name

 Name of the mod, no spaces. Allowed characters: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ 

 description

 A short description of the mod, shown on the mod list. Max 250 characters.

 version_number

 Version number of the mod, following the semantic version format Major.Minor.Patch

 dependencies

 A list of other packages that are required for this package to function.

 Max length of a name is 128 characters and it cannot contain characters other than abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_ .

 Description 
 Short description of the package, will be displayed in list views and other views where a full length readme cannot be shown. 250 characters max.
 Version Number 
 The version number of the package, following the 3-numbered Major.Minor.Patch semantic version format.
 For example, version 1.3.2 is newer than 1.2.23 but older than 2.1.0 . Be mindful that these are not decimal numbers, and adding an extra zero at the end is significant. For example 1.0.10 is 9 patch versions higher than 1.0.1 . Each version number part is a full number.
 
 Thunderstore will always display the highest package version regardless of upload date

 To update a package, simply increment its version number and re-upload it.

 Dependencies declared in the manifest are automatically installed by the mod manager when a package is installed.
 The dependencies field should be a list of strings, each string being a reference to a valid Thunderstore package.

These packages are still considered malware even if the author discloses that they contain such capabilities. **A few examples of packages that are malware:** * A package that secretly collects personal information on people who use it. * A package called "Furry Fun Pack" that purposely crashes your game when you launch it. * A package called "One Million Fish" that adds new fish to the game, but also bans a player named Steve from any server with the mod. * A package called "Bananas" that adds bananas to the game, but also closes your game if you live in China. **A few examples of packages that aren't necessarily malware:** * A package called "Your game closes if you die" that closes your game if you die. * A package called "Secure Server Banlist" that bans Steve and his friends from connecting to any server with the mod. ## NSFW Content **All packages containing NSFW content must have the "Contains NSFW content" option selected.** Sexually explicit content such as nudity is not allowed in the icon, README, changelog, or any other file that gets displayed on the Thunderstore website or mod manager. ## Compatibility and the Ecosystem Where possible, packages should not contain obfuscated code (or execute code downloaded from external sources). # thunderstore-cli

[![Build & Test](https://github.com/thunderstore-io/thunderstore-cli/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thunderstore-io/thunderstore-cli/actions/workflows/test.yml)

[![NuGet Package](https://img.shields.io/nuget/v/tcli)](https://www.nuget.org/packages/tcli)
[![downloads](https://img.shields.io/nuget/dt/tcli)](https://www.nuget.org/packages/tcli)

Thunderstore CLI (just "TCLI" from here on) is a command line tool for building and uploading mod packages to
[Thunderstore](https://thunderstore.io/) mod database, and installing mods via the command line.

## Installation
If all you're interested in is the package building/publishing capabilities of TCLI, then you can simply do:
```
dotnet tool install -g tcli
```
In your command line of choice, which will install the tool via NuGet.
This version doesn't come with the mod installation functionality however.

Otherwise, just download the latest release from [here](https://github.com/thunderstore-io/thunderstore-cli/releases) and extract the ZIP wherever you'll be using TCLI.

## Usage
For building packages, see [the wiki](https://github.com/thunderstore-io/thunderstore-cli/wiki).

For managing mods via TCLI, see the next section.
## Mod Management

### Installation
TCLI will automatically download and install mods in the correct format for you, and will run the game with whatever arguments your mod loader requires.

For all of these commands, `tcli.exe` can be swapped for `./tcli` on Linux. Everything else should be the same.

To get started, import your game from the Thunderstore API using:
```
tcli.exe import-game {game identifier, e.g. ror2 or valheim}
```
To run the game from a specific file instead of say, through Steam (you probably want this for servers!) use `--exepath {path/to/server/launcher.exe}`. Passing in a script file also works fine.

To install mods, use the command:
```
tcli.exe install {game identifier} {namespace-modname(-version)}
```
You can also add `--profile ProfileName` to set a custom name for the profile. By default it uses the name `DefaultProfile`.

Mod uninstalls are done in a similar fashion:
```
tcli.exe uninstall {game identifier} {namespace-modname}
```
And running the game is done with:
```
tcli.exe run {game identifier}
```
The `--profile` snippet from above still applies to both of those commands.

If you want to run the game with a specific set of arguments, you can use `--args "--flag parameter1 parameter2"`

The installed mods by default will go into `%APPDATA%\ThunderstoreCLI` on Windows and `~/.config/ThunderstoreCLI` on Linux. This is configurable by using `--tcli-directory` with any command.

The ThunderstoreCLI directory will contain a file called `GameDefintions.json`, which contains metadata about the configured games, the profiles for each game, and a copy of the manifests of each installed mod. You shouldn't normally be editing this manually.

The same directory also contains a cache for mod ZIPS named `ModCache`, the actual profile files in a folder called `Profiles`, and a caches for the API responses from the Thunderstore API for packages.

A valid package is a zip file that contains the following files:

icon.png PNG icon for the mod, must be 256x256 resolution.

"Hello world"

### File storage (MinIO)

Local development uses [MinIO](https://github.com/minio/minio) for S3-compatible
file storage, available at <http://thunderstore.localhost:9000/> with
`thunderstore` / `thunderstore` credentials.

### REST API

Swagger documentation is served at `/api/docs/`. The primary endpoint is
`/api/v1/package/`, which lists all active mods; a single mod can be fetched from
`/api/v1/package/{uuid4}/`, where `{uuid4}` is the mod's UUID.

## Testing

```bash
# Run the test suite
docker compose exec django pytest

# Recreate the test database (e.g. after model changes)
docker compose exec django pytest --create-db --migrations
```

CI fails a pull request if it lowers test coverage. To check coverage locally
before submitting:

```bash
docker compose exec django coverage run -m pytest
docker compose exec django coverage report -m
```

### Test duration estimates

CI splits the test run across workers by expected duration, so the duration
database should be refreshed occasionally:

```bash
docker compose exec django pytest --store-durations
```

## Production configuration

The settings below are for **deployments** — local development needs almost none
of them, since the dev defaults live in `docker-compose.yml` and `.env.template`.
See
[`django/thunderstore/core/settings.py`](django/thunderstore/core/settings.py) for
the full set of supported variables.

### General

-   `DEBUG`: Leave unset or `false` in production.

# Thunderstore legal/policy research — findings

## Headline: **There is no Thunderstore Terms of Service. At all.**

This is the single most important finding. I verified it five independent ways. Everything downstream (A–D) follows from it.

---

## G. First — the `/tos/` question (answering this first because it reframes everything)

**`https://thunderstore.io/tos/` does NOT return a Cloudflare 403. It returns a genuine HTTP 404.**

- `curl -s -A "<browser UA>" https://thunderstore.io/tos/` → **HTTP 404**, and the SPA shell embeds the router's own error payload verbatim:
  > `"status",404,"statusText","Not Found","internal",true,"data","Error: No route matches URL \"/tos\""`
- `WebFetch` on the same URL → `The server returned HTTP 404 Not Found.`
- `https://old.thunderstore.io/tos/` → **HTTP 404**, Django's 404 page, quoted verbatim:
  > "Page not found — The page you are looking for has either never existed, or it has been removed. If the problem persists and you require immediate assistance, please head to our Discord server and contact an administrator." — https://old.thunderstore.io/tos/

The `old.thunderstore.io/tos/` link you may have seen in the page source is **not a ToS link** — it is the site's "switch to legacy site" button, which mirrors whatever path you're currently on. On `/tos/` it just happened to render as `old.thunderstore.io/tos/`.

### Corroboration that no ToS exists anywhere

1. **Internet Archive CDX** for `thunderstore.io/tos*` returns **zero records ever** — the page has never existed.
2. **The live footers.** New site (`https://thunderstore.io/c/repo/`) — the only legal-ish links in the entire DOM are `https://pages.thunderstore.io/p/contact-us` and `https://pages.thunderstore.io/p/privacy-policy`. Old site footer: "About: Contact Us | Privacy Policy | Thunderstore Wiki — Developers: API Docs | GitHub Repo". **No Terms of Service link on either site.**
3. **The codebase.** Thunderstore is AGPL-3.0 open source. There is a Django app `django/thunderstore/legal/` that serves legal contracts at `/legal/c/<slug>/`, and `base.html` renders a footer "Legal" column only `{% if legal_contracts %}`. Since no Legal column renders on the live site, **zero legal contracts are published**. I probed `/legal/c/tos/`, `/legal/c/terms-of-service/`, `/legal/c/terms/`, `/legal/c/privacy-policy/`, `/legal/c/acceptable-use/`, `/legal/c/content-policy/` → **all 404**.
4. **Grep of the full repo** (`git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/thunderstore-io/Thunderstore`) for `terms of (use|service)`, `you (hereby )?grant`, `license to`, `agree to`, `redistribut` across `.py/.html/.ts/.tsx/.md` → **zero hits**. Same grep on `thunderstore-ui` file tree → no tos/terms/legal/policy files.
5. **No ToS subpages exist.** `pages.thunderstore.io/p/terms-of-service`, `/p/tos`, and `pages.thunderstore.io/` root all → **404**. The only two pages that exist on that host are `/p/privacy-policy` and `/p/contact-us` (confirmed by archive.org CDX too). There is no `/tos/acceptable-use/`, `/tos/content-policy/`, `/tos/dmca/`, or `/tos/api-terms/`.

**The one dangling reference:** the Privacy Policy cites a ToS that is not published anywhere:
> "To access and manage the content you post on our website, including removing illegal, harmful and abusive content. ... Processing is necessary for our legitimate interest to provide you a safe service and **to abide by our Terms of Services**." — https://pages.thunderstore.io/p/privacy-policy

---

## The complete set of documents that DO exist

| Document | URL | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Privacy Policy | https://pages.thunderstore.io/p/privacy-policy | Live, full text retrieved |
| Contact Us | https://pages.thunderstore.io/p/contact-us | Live |
| Global Rules (moderation) | https://wiki.thunderstore.io/moderation/global-rules | Live — **this is the closest thing to a content policy** |
| Removing a Package | https://wiki.thunderstore.io/moderation/removing-a-package | Live — closest thing to takedown policy |
| Creating a Package (manifest spec) | https://wiki.thunderstore.io/mods/creating-a-package | Live |
| Brand guidelines "Terms" | https://github.com/thunderstore-io/brand-guidelines | Live — **only binding-sounding terms I found** |
| API docs (Swagger) | https://thunderstore.io/api/docs/ | Live, no terms attached |
| robots.txt | https://thunderstore.io/robots.txt | Live |

Legal entity, from the Privacy Policy:
> "The data controller for the processing described in this notice is: **Riskidev Oy**" — https://pages.thunderstore.io/p/privacy-policy

Contact routing, quoted verbatim from https://pages.thunderstore.io/p/contact-us:
> "**Business Inquiries** — For business inquiries, please reach out to us via email at contact@thunderstore.io
> **Legal** — For legal matters, please reach out to us via email at legal@thunderstore.io"

---

## A. Mandatory license grant from uploaders to Thunderstore / downstream users?

**NOT FOUND / NOT ADDRESSED.** There is no such clause because there is no ToS. There is no uploader agreement, no "you grant us a worldwide non-exclusive license", no sublicensing-to-users clause, no redistribution grant — nothing.

I verified there is no click-through agreement on upload either: `django/thunderstore/repository/templates/repository/package_create.html` and `package_create_old.html` contain **no** "agree"/"terms"/"license" text, and the manifest serializer (`ManifestV1Serializer` in `django/thunderstore/repository/package_manifest.py`) has no licensing field or acknowledgement.

**Practical consequence for you:** Thunderstore has no contractual chain of title to pass to you. Whatever redistribution right you have for any given package comes **only from that package author's own license**, if they declared one (see B).

The closest thing in any Thunderstore-controlled document is the Global Rules, quoted in full:

> ## Copyright and Licensing
> Copyright laws and code licensing must be followed where applicable.
> * Do not distribute game files such as Assembly-CSharp.dll, unless given explicit permission by the game's developers.
> * Do not reupload packages or assets by other authors unless you have permission to redistribute them or are following their licensing.

— https://wiki.thunderstore.io/moderation/global-rules

Note this rule is aimed at *uploaders reuploading to Thunderstore*, not at downstream redistributors, but it's the platform's stated posture on redistribution: permission-or-license required.

---

## B. Default/assumed license if the author declares nothing?

**There is none. There is no license field in the manifest spec at all, and no default is stated anywhere.**

The manifest.json spec, quoted verbatim from https://wiki.thunderstore.io/mods/creating-a-package:

> The `manifest.json` file is what tells Thunderstore and other tools some critical technical information about your package (such as the name & version). Some of it may also be used for presentation.
> The file should be in standard JSON format (UTF-8 encoded) with the following contents:
>
> | Key | Description |
> |---|---|
> | `name` | Name of the mod, no spaces. Allowed characters: `a-z A-Z 0-9 _` |
> | `description` | A short description of the mod, shown on the mod list. Max 250 characters. |
> | `version_number` | Version number of the mod, following the semantic version format Major.Minor.Patch |
> | `dependencies` | A list of other packages that are required for this package to function. |
> | `website_url` | URL of the mod's website (e.g. GitHub repo). Can be left an empty string. |

Full example, verbatim from the same page:
```json
{
    "name": "TestMod",
    "version_number": "1.1.0",
    "website_url": "https://github.com/thunderstore-io",
    "description": "This is a description for a mod. 250 characters max",
    "dependencies": [
        "MythicManiac-TestMod-1.1.0"
    ]
}
```

**That is the whole spec. There is no `license` key, no `license_url`, no SPDX field.** I confirmed against the server-side validator `ManifestV1Serializer` (`django/thunderstore/repository/package_manifest.py`), whose complete field list is: `name`, `version_number`, `website_url`, `description`, `dependencies`, and an optional `installers`. Nothing else.

(`installers` is undocumented on the live wiki — it only appears in the now-redirected legacy template `django/thunderstore/repository/templates/repository/package_docs.html`, which says: *"A list of installer declarations. Installer declarations can be used to explicitly control how a mod manager should install the package. If omitted, legacy install rules are automatically used. ... This field will become mandatory in the future."*)

### README requirements — quoted verbatim

> A valid Thunderstore package is a zip file which must contain at least the following files at the root of the zip:
> | Name | Description |
> |---|---|
> | `icon.png` | PNG icon for the mod, must be 256x256 resolution. |
> | `README.md` | Readme in markdown syntax. Will be rendered on the package's page. |
> | `manifest.json` | JSON file with metadata of the package. See Manifest for structure. |
>
> Packages can also contain a `CHANGELOG.md`
> **File naming is case-sensitive and must match the above exactly!**

> Currently there's a maximum package size limit of 5 242 880 000 bytes (or roughly 5 GB), but this is a soft-limit and can be increased if needed.

> The readme supports markdown syntax, closely but not exactly matching that of GitHub's. ... The readme has to be UTF-8 compatible

— all https://wiki.thunderstore.io/mods/creating-a-package

**A README is mandatory; a license declaration is not required, not requested, and has no home in the format.** In practice a license, if any, lives in free-text inside README.md or in the linked `website_url` repo — machine-unreadable.

Note the icon guidance explicitly anticipates third-party consumers:
> "Transparency is supported, although if used, it is recommended the icon has clear borders that work with any background color as icons might be displayed in a variety of themes (**e.g. with 3rd party mod managers**)."

---

## C. API usage, automated access, scraping, indexing, mirroring, rate limits, attribution

**No terms exist.** But there are three affirmative signals that the API is *designed* for exactly what you want to do, plus one machine-readable restriction.

**The one actual restriction — robots.txt**, quoted in full from https://thunderstore.io/robots.txt:
```
User-agent: *
Disallow: /auth/
Allow: /api/docs/
Disallow: /api/
Sitemap: https://thunderstore.io/sitemap.xml
```
`Disallow: /api/` applies to crawlers, not to an API client. But it is the only written statement anywhere about automated access, and it is worth noting you should not present your server-side fetcher as a crawler.

**The API explicitly instructs third parties to construct download URLs themselves.** From the live OpenAPI schema (`https://thunderstore.io/api/docs/?format=openapi`), `GET /api/experimental/package-index/`:
> "Response is a stream of newline delimited JSON.
> Download links are not included in the response. **The client is expected to build them using the following pattern:** `https://thunderstore.io/package/download/{namespace}/{name}/{version_number}/`"

**The API explicitly supports local caching / mirroring.** From the same schema:
- `GET /api/experimental/package/wikis/`: *"Fetch a bulk of package wikis at once. **Supports querying by update time to accommodate local caching.**"*
- `GET /c/{community_identifier}/api/v1/package-listing-index/`: *"Redirects to a gzip compressed blob file containing an array of URLs. Each URL points to a gzip compressed chunk of the community's package listing... The response supports conditional requests via the `If-Modified-Since` header, in which case a 304 is returned instead of a redirect."*

**Schema disclaimer**, verbatim: `"description": "Schema is automatically generated and not completely accurate."`, with the only listed contact being their Discord.

**Rate limits / User-Agent:** **NOT FOUND / NOT ADDRESSED.** No documented rate limit, no quota, no API key requirement, no required User-Agent, no attribution requirement anywhere. I grepped the whole backend for `throttl|ratelimit|rate_limit|user.agent` — the only DRF throttles in the codebase are on *profile creation* (`LegacyProfileCreateThrottle`) and a download-metrics dedup; **no throttling on the read/listing/download endpoints**.

I verified empirically with a deliberately non-browser UA (`curl-test/1.0`):
- `GET /api/experimental/package/Kesomannen/GaleModManager/` → 200 JSON, no auth.
- `GET /c/repo/api/v1/package-listing-index/` → 302 to `gcdn.thunderstore.io`, `cache-control: public, max-age=0, s-maxage=300`, `cf-cache-status: HIT`.
- `HEAD /package/download/bbepis/BepInExPack/5.4.2100/` → 302 to `https://gcdn.thunderstore.io/live/repository/packages/bbepis-BepInExPack-5.4.2100.zip`, no auth, no UA check, `cf-cache-status: BYPASS`.

Downloads are Cloudflare-fronted over a GCore CDN. Nothing blocked me.

---

## D. Restriction on commercial use (paid hosting company using the API/packages in a paid product)?

**NOT FOUND / NOT ADDRESSED.** There is no commercial-use clause, no non-commercial restriction, no "personal use only", no reseller clause, no API licensing tier — because there is no ToS or API terms document.

The only thing in the ballpark, and it is about **trademark/brand assets, not the API or packages**, quoted in full from https://github.com/thunderstore-io/brand-guidelines (README.md, `master` branch):

> ## Terms
> - Don't claim to be officially affiliated with the Thunderstore project unless explicitly given permission to do so.
> - Don't use the assets for purposes which aren't related to the Thunderstore ecosystem.
> - If you're uncertain about your use case, ask and we'll clarify!

(Fuller guidance is in `thunderstore-brand-kit.pdf` in that repo, which I did not parse.)

Context on how Thunderstore itself thinks about money, from their own blog — https://blog.thunderstore.io/p/2023-monetization-survey-results:
> "Some of our early stage competitors (such as modrinth or mod.io) have sought out funding from VC investors; an option that has also been available to us, but one we've wanted to hold out on at least for now. Thunderstore is still majority owned by the dev team... Soon we will be launching a subscription option that will offer some benefits, such as an ad-free experience, a profile badge, and early access to the upcoming website redesign."

Relevant because Thunderstore's revenue is ads + subscriptions served on their own surfaces. A third-party catalog UI that mirrors metadata and serves it ad-free structurally bypasses their monetization. There is no rule against it — but it is the most likely source of friction, and it is exactly the kind of thing the `legal@thunderstore.io` address exists for.

---

## E. Position on third-party mod managers / launchers

**There is no written policy blessing or restricting them. But their conduct is an unambiguous, documented endorsement.** Evidence, strongest first:

**1. Thunderstore owns and publishes r2modman.** `r2modmanPlus` is a repository in the `thunderstore-io` GitHub org — https://github.com/thunderstore-io/r2modmanPlus, described by them as *"A simple and easy to use mod manager for several games using Thunderstore"*. The upstream is `ebkr/r2modmanPlus`, and Thunderstore's own wiki routes users to it for canonical packaging rules:
> "Documentation for the default (legacy) behavior is currently maintained as a wiki page on **the r2modmanPlus wiki**" — `django/thunderstore/repository/templates/repository/package_docs.html`

**2. Thunderstore distributes competing third-party managers on its own store.** `Kesomannen/GaleModManager` (Gale) is a live, listed, downloadable package on thunderstore.io — verified via `GET /api/experimental/package/Kesomannen/GaleModManager/` → 200. So is `ebkr/r2modman`. Thunderstore hosts its competitors' clients.

**3. Their own CLI is explicitly framed as being for third-party tooling.** From https://blog.thunderstore.io/p/2022-in-review:
> "We've made massive strides in improving our desktop tooling over the past year with the introduction of thunderstore-cli. This tool, in short, allows you to install, author, and otherwise manage your mod installs without leaving the comfort of your terminal. **It hosts the same functionality as the Thunderstore Mod Manager, but in a form ready for use by community tooling.**"

**4. Their own CLI explicitly targets game servers — your exact use case.** From https://github.com/thunderstore-io/thunderstore-cli README:
> "TCLI will automatically download and install mods in the correct format for you, and will run the game with whatever arguments your mod loader requires."
> "To run the game from a specific file instead of say, through Steam (**you probably want this for servers!**) use `--exepath {path/to/server/launcher.exe}`"

**5. Install-rule metadata is published as a public schema for third parties.** From https://wiki.thunderstore.io/mods/packaging-your-mods:
> "For a full list of install rules for each game, check the ecosystem-schema" → https://github.com/thunderstore-io/ecosystem-schema/tree/master/games/data

**6. The package format docs assume third-party managers will render their assets** ("e.g. with 3rd party mod managers", quoted in B above).

**Caveat on the first-party manager:** Thunderstore Mod Manager is distributed via Overwolf (`https://get.thunderstore.io/` 302s to `https://www.overwolf.com/app/thunderstore-thunderstore_mod_manager`, "Free / Contains Ads / Subscription available", 21.3M downloads). TSMM is ad-supported. That is another data point on where their commercial sensitivity sits — but again, **no written restriction on third parties exists.**

---

## F. DMCA / takedown / content-liability language

**There is no DMCA policy, no designated agent, no takedown procedure document, and no safe-harbour notice.** I grepped the entire backend for `dmca|takedown|copyright` — the only hit in the whole codebase is a report-reason enum in `django/thunderstore/ts_reports/consts.py`:

```python
REPORT_REASON_CHOICES = [
    {"value": "Spam", "label": "Spam"},
    {"value": "Malware", "label": "Suspected malware"},
    {"value": "Reupload", "label": "Unauthorized reupload"},
    {"value": "CopyrightOrLicense", "label": "Copyright / License issue"},
    {"value": "WrongCommunity", "label": "Wrong community"},
    {"value": "WrongCategories", "label": "Wrong categories"},
    {"value": "Other", "label": "Other"},
]
```

The nearest thing to a takedown policy is the removal doc, quoted verbatim from https://wiki.thunderstore.io/moderation/removing-a-package:

> ## Rejection
> Moderators can **reject** listings in their community. Rejection is used specifically for removing packages that break global or community rules, or when requested by the package's author.
> * The website page for a rejected listing will 404 in the community it was rejected from. This does not apply to moderators and members of the team that uploaded the package.
> * The package will no longer appear in the mod manager's mod list (**but it will not be automatically removed for people who have already downloaded it**).
> * Rejected mods will not be downloaded as dependencies.
>
> ## Deletion
> If necessary, Thunderstore administrators can **delete** a package completely. This is usually reserved for packages that contain illegal content or other serious issues.
>
> ## Deprecation
> * Deprecated means a package is no longer functional OR should not be used anymore for any reason...
> * Deprecated mods can still be found on the website and mod manager by checking a box in the search options.
> * **Deprecated mods will still be downloaded as dependencies.**

**This is the operationally critical bit for you:** rejection/deletion propagates as a **404 or a disappearance from the listing index**, with no removal signal, no tombstone, no takedown feed. If you cache metadata or mirror .zips, a package removed for malware or copyright infringement will keep working in your mirror indefinitely unless you re-verify against the live index. And the deprecation/rejection distinction matters for your dependency resolver: deprecated packages still resolve as dependencies, rejected ones do not.

### Global Rules in full (the de-facto content policy)

From https://wiki.thunderstore.io/moderation/global-rules — the sections most relevant to you redistributing this content into paying customers' servers:

> **Unlawful Content** — Packages that contain unlawful content are not allowed.

> **Malware** — Packages containing malware are not allowed. Packages that deceptively disrupt or damage other software or hardware are considered malware. This includes keyloggers, crypto miners, token stealers, and other malicious programs. These packages are still considered malware even if the author discloses that they contain such capabilities.

> **NSFW Content** — All packages containing NSFW content must have the "Contains NSFW content" option selected. Sexually explicit content such as nudity is not allowed in the icon, README, changelog, or any other file that gets displayed on the Thunderstore website or mod manager.

> **Compatibility and the Ecosystem** — Where possible, packages should not contain obfuscated code (or execute code downloaded from external sources). Obfuscation makes it difficult to audit malicious behavior and fix incompatibilities with other packages. Packages should rely on external mod managers for updates, rather than be capable of updating themselves.

> **Harassment and Abuse** / **Spam** / **AI Generated Content** — [full text at the URL; includes "Untested or non-functional AI-generated mods" as spam, and "A package with AI generated assets or code should be given the `AI Generated` category"]

Two things jump out for a hosting panel: (a) the malware rule is **reactive** — packages are removed after report/review, so at any moment your mirror may be serving something that has not yet been caught; (b) the NSFW flag is a **self-declared manifest/upload option** that you would need to honour in your catalog UI, and it's carried on the listing, not in manifest.json.

Site-wide notice currently rendered on old.thunderstore.io, verbatim:
> "Please disclose if any significant portion of your mod was created using AI tools by adding the 'AI Generated' category. Failing to do so may result in the mod being removed from Thunderstore."

---

## Bottom line for your two use cases

**(a) Indexing/mirroring metadata + icons.** No terms forbid it; the API is explicitly built for it (`If-Modified-Since` conditional requests, chunked listing index, "supports querying by update time to accommodate local caching"). But `robots.txt` says `Disallow: /api/` for crawlers, there is no attribution requirement to comply with, and the brand-guidelines "Terms" mean you must not imply official affiliation if you use their logo. The real exposure is not legal — it's that ad-free mirroring routes around their only revenue model, and there's no contract telling you where the line is.

**(b) Downloading .zips server-side and installing into customers' servers.** Technically unrestricted and unauthenticated (verified). Thunderstore's own CLI does this and explicitly supports the server case. **But**: Thunderstore grants you nothing, because there is no ToS and therefore no license grant (A). There is no default license (B) and no license field in the manifest (B), so for most packages you cannot mechanically determine whether you have the right to redistribute the bits to a paying customer. Their own Global Rules state the standard they hold uploaders to — *"Do not reupload packages or assets by other authors unless you have permission to redistribute them or are following their licensing"* — and a paid hosting panel serving copies is closer to that than to a end-user mod manager fetching on a user's behalf.

Two design mitigations worth considering, both supported by what I found: fetch from `thunderstore.io/package/download/...` **per-install at request time** rather than mirroring .zips (keeps you a fetch proxy, keeps download counts accruing to authors, and means rejections/deletions propagate as 404s rather than being silently cached); and re-validate cached metadata against the listing index so removed packages drop out of your catalog. Then send one email to `legal@thunderstore.io` (their stated legal channel) describing the paid-hosting use case before launch — given there is no document to rely on, a written reply from them is the only thing that would give you anything to stand on.

**Things I explicitly could not find:** a ToS; any ToS subpage (acceptable use, content policy, DMCA, API terms); a license grant; a default license; a manifest `license` field; any rate limit, quota, User-Agent or attribution requirement; any commercial-use restriction on the API or packages; any written statement about third-party mod managers.
